title: Documentation Review (run 7, trend vs 2026-10-21): both repos, 821cf841→HEAD; first doc run to feed the area notes and review them as a doc surface
description:
## As asked

<!-- harbour-periodical-gate id="documentation-review" -->
**Documentation Review, run 7 (trend vs the 2026-10-21 report).** This is the drift-first documentation periodical (`documentation-review` in `lib/periodicals.js`). **This task is the review itself.** You write the report and its area-note entries, merge them in one docs-only PR, get the second read, comment and close. You mint no follow-up tickets.

Repositories: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour, "LV") and JKershaw/simple-dispatcher ("SD"). Both are in scope, as in every earlier run of this series.

## What was found when this task was minted (2026-11-10). Re-check all of it at HEAD.

**The window.**

* **LV:** `821cf841e84ef0b151f545321902fcd12e2b7b1a..f5b1f5efa25265a49cb3c6ca04879610fcc278f9` (the previous report's measured commit to HEAD at minting). That is 461 commits. Mapped through `docs/areas/areas.json`, production files touched per area are: runs-and-dispatch 79, front-end-pages 74, front-end-browser 73, llm-and-prompts 55, web-routes 37, auth-accounts-and-workspaces 33, agent-api 27, other-features 20, reports-and-operator-tools 13, providers 11, platform-and-plumbing 7, task-model 2, wiring 1. About 5,000 more changed files are docs, tests and evidence (mostly `docs/reviews/`, `docs/papers/`, `tests/`). Recompute all of this, and include any commits after `f5b1f5efa`.
* **SD:** `bb1da78e29a99940dc5aa37cf7e826992db097f5..5d8489e7fd8434f0e69af7df11a3746790abbe64`. That is 67 commits. By SD's registry: test-harnesses 50, state-and-config 9, launch-and-harnesses 6, stop-hook-and-relay 6, reapers-and-liveness 5, loop-and-routing 3, plus 176 docs and unit-test files.

**The previous edition.** `docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-10-21.md` (LIN-3744, PR #2028). Its two minted tickets are Done: M1 LIN-3745 (LIN-3300 meta-prompt residue) and M2 LIN-3746 (SD enumeration census guards, which added `test/doc-enumeration-census.test.js`, `test/module-map-census.test.js` and `test/phases-doc-census.test.js`). Confirm both fixes held, and then carry every other finding forward with a delta. Spot checks at minting, to re-verify and not to trust:

* #2: `docs/dispatch-integration.md` still says the runner kit sends `POST /api/proxy/runner/heartbeat` (LIN-3636, Backlog).
* #3: `CLAUDE.md` still says "landing page with static projects preview" (LIN-2391, Backlog).
* #5: the gate codes `PERIODICAL_REPORT_NOT_PERSISTED` and `PERIODICAL_ADVERSARIAL_READ_NOT_RECORDED` (`lib/periodical-report-gate.js`) still have 0 hits in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `docs/proxy-integration.md` and `public/llms.txt`. This task's own Done transition runs through that gate (LIN-2390, Backlog).
* #6: `docs/architecture/source-map.md` grew again, from 153,272 B to 193,379 B (414 lines). It is still the human decision between generating and pinning the map.
* #7: `effort` on POST /dispatch (LIN-2656). #8: post-split `routes/proxy.js` citations, still in about 10 docs (LIN-3116). #11: hand-counted figures (LIN-3115). #14: the CI-doc twin, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/architecture/ci.md` "unit and e2e jobs". #12: the `docs/runbooks/improvement-cycles.md` "until LIN-3661" line. Also #9 env drift, #10 auth.md, #15 stale inline comments, #16 H9–H12, #17 executive-summary framing (LIN-3510), #18 SD.
* Other open doc owners: LIN-2390, 2391, 3115, 3116, 2656, 3510, 3636, 4320 (the enqueue route list in `CLAUDE.md` misses `POST /periodicals/{id}/mint`), plus the "known-owned" list in the 10-21 report. Check each one's state before you cite it. A finding already filed as a ticket stays in the report only.

**What is new since the last run, and has never been doc-reviewed:**

* **Area notes** in both repos (LIN-4347/4371/4372/4379/4380/4383): `docs/areas/README.md`, `areas.json` and the per-area notes, with guards `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (LV) and `test/area-notes.test.js` (SD), plus `tests/unit/lin-4377-area-notes-pointer-bytes.test.js`. These are now a doc surface that agents read before every change. Review them for accuracy, duplication between the two READMEs, and inflation. Drift & Coherence run 6 (`docs/reviews/drift-coherence-review-2026-11-10.md`, P1–P4) owns the *decision-duplication* angle. The *doc accuracy and readability* angle is yours.
* **The** `## As asked` **seal and the** `## Size of the move` **record** (LIN-4351 to 4369, LIN-4393 removed a setting) and the **leftover step** (LIN-4373 to 4377, `LEFTOVER_RULE` in `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js`). Check the proxy catalog, the guide, `CLAUDE.md` and `public/llms.txt` against the code, and look for residue from the removed setting.
* **The per-credential rate limit and the broker 429 policy** (LIN-4378/4384/4385, in both repos), the landed periodical state (LIN-4381), periodical scope (LIN-4382) and the periodical mint route (LIN-4313). Are they documented, and is that documentation correct?
* **Doc stores that grew in the window:** `docs/reviews/` is 91 MB with 109 top-level reports and still no index; `docs/papers/` is 38 MB; `experiments/` is 22 MB. The 10-21 report recorded the missing index as a human call. Reassess it subtractively.

**Budgets at minting:** LV `CLAUDE.md` is 110 lines / 11,976 B against 110 / 12,000 (`tests/unit/claude-md-line-budget.test.js`), so any fix there must remove as much as it adds. SD `CLAUDE.md` is 89 lines / 5,022 B. LV area notes `runs-and-dispatch.md` (6,143 B) and `llm-and-prompts.md` (6,142 B) are at the 6,144 B cap, so any entry you add there must be paid for by pruning or distilling.

## Audit the scope before you run it

Treat everything above as a starting point to widen, not a checklist to stay inside. Before you review, look for surfaces that are in remit but not listed here, and fold them in. A scope you could only shrink is suspect. Stay **broad in discovery but bounded in output**. The wider scope changes only what you *examine*:

* The report stays uncapped and severity-ranked. A clean or near-empty result is a genuine outcome.
* The note writes stay within their existing bound: add an entry only where a finding binds a builder or waits in an area, and keep each note under its cap.

Places to start widening:

* The seams with sibling reviews (all in `lib/periodicals.js`). Contract *behaviour* belongs to API Quality, module rationale to Comprehension-Debt, decision duplication to Drift & Coherence, the rendered first run to Onboarding, and rendering to Design & Interface. A doc surface that none of them owns is yours. The 10-21 report named `public/llms.txt` beyond H11 as the largest unswept surface, and said the 2,990-line `docs/proxy-integration.md` was only spot-checked.
* Prompt text served to agents as documentation: `lib/prompts/`, `lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, the runner kickoff and `docs/runner-prompt.md`.
* SD's `README.md`, now 415 lines / 35 KB, and SD's undocumented env vars (48 at the last count).

## Read prior runs first

Read `docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-10-21.md` in full, and the 09-26 report's trend items. Build on them. Do not re-derive the same report, and do not re-flag what is handled. Skim the window's sibling reports in `docs/reviews/` for doc findings they handed off without a ticket. The 10-21 report recorded a pattern of sibling hand-offs that had no owner.

## Run the review (drift first)

Write for two audiences, developers and AI agents.

* **Accuracy and drift.** Treat each doc claim as a hypothesis. Locate the concrete thing it asserts (a path, export, route, CLI flag, env var, request/response shape, selector) and verify it against source at HEAD. Take counts by **executing** source, not by grep, as the 10-21 run did. A disagreement on wording is a drift finding. A disagreement on intent is a human-decision flag.
* **README and entry-point quality.** Do `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/agent-onboarding.md` orient a newcomer fast, without drowning them?
* **Inline comments.** Do they explain *why*? Flag both non-obvious code that has no rationale and comments that are stale or misleading.
* **API and interface docs.** Check the endpoints, commands and exports this project exposes: inputs, outputs, errors, auth and scope. Cover the served catalog, the guide, `public/llms.txt` and the runner-kit contract.
* **Quality, assessed subtractively.** Look at redundancy, organisation, discoverability and readability. The fixes are consolidate, tighten, relocate or delete, not net-new prose. Unjustified doc growth (inflation) is a finding in its own right.

These classes are examples, not a limit. Find the full set for this remit from the repo. A class list is a floor to build on, never a ceiling to stay inside.

## Write an uncapped report

Put it at `docs/reviews/documentation-review-<run date>.md` in LinearViewer. That is the series convention, and it covers both repos. Record both HEADs. Rank findings by severity and ground each one at HEAD, not in prior prose. Do not pad, cap or invent make-work. Nothing, one or several findings are all valid outcomes. Keep the report table-first; the 10-21 report is a good model. If evidence is large, it goes in a `docs/reviews/_evidence-<date>-docs/` folder, following the sibling precedent.

## Feed the area notes, and mint no follow-up tasks

Follow the notes' own rules, not any assumed here. Read `docs/areas/README.md` in each repo: the registry, the note format, the guard, the 6,144 B cap, and the one home for each leftover (`LEFTOVER_RULE`).

1. Start from the window above. Map each changed file to its area through the registry, and look first where work landed.
2. In each note you touch, prune entries that are settled or no longer true, and distil so the note stays under its cap.
3. A finding that leaves work in an area becomes a **Waiting** entry. A rule a builder there must follow becomes a **Lesson**.
4. Each entry cites the area's file first, names its source as "Documentation Review, <run date>", and cites this report second.
5. LV notes cover only code paths. A doc finding cites the code that owns the doc first (see the README).
6. SD notes may not cite LV paths in backticks. LV-side and SD-side entries go in the repo where the cited file lives, and the report links them.
7. Commit the report and the LV note edits together in **one docs-only PR**: rebase it onto main, get `ci-success` and the notes guard green, and merge it.
8. If SD notes need edits, open a second docs-only PR in SD and say so in the report. Seams have no full home in the notes yet. File a cross-repo or cross-area seam under the area a change would start from, name the other side, and say this plainly in the report.

## Route each finding that has no area note to the person, never to a ticket

* **A larger tidy** (for example the `source-map.md` generate-or-pin decision, or a `docs/reviews/` index): write it as a Waiting entry worded as a size of move, and also list it in the closing comment.
* **A finding with no area file to cite** (manifests, lockfiles, or a live secret): put it in the closing comment, addressed to the person.

## Stay review-only

Change no code, config, secrets or docs, except the report (with its evidence) and the area-note edits.

## Adversarial second read (required before Done)

After the report and its note edits are written, a genuinely separate reader must answer, cold: *"what is the largest item in this window that this report missed or misfiled?"*

* **Tier 1** (preferred) is a wholly separate session. **Tier 2** (accepted) is a fresh-context sub-agent. **Tier 3** (a self re-read) is not accepted. State the tier you used.
* Post one comment on this task that holds all three of these lines together:
  * `Adversarial second-read verdict: AGREE` or `Adversarial second-read verdict: DISAGREE`
  * `Differed from top finding: YES` or `Differed from top finding: NO`
  * `Disposition: fixed in place`, `Disposition: escalated` or `Disposition: no change`
* Copy the same three fields, the tier, the question and the reader's answer **in full** into a `## Adversarial Second-Read` section of the report. The 10-21 run lost the reader's verbatim answer, so retain it this time.
* AGREE and DISAGREE both conclude normally. A DISAGREE is itself the escalation.

## Conclude

1. Merge the report PR once its required checks are green. If merging is genuinely impossible, name the blocker in the closing comment as an explicit handoff.
2. Post a concise, severity-ranked summary comment on this task. It links the report and names the PR(s). It lists, for the person, every larger tidy and every finding with no area file to cite.
3. Move this task to Done.

Do not leave the task open. A review task left open is re-recommended indefinitely.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Finish line superseded (LIN-4390)

This task was minted at 09:37 UTC on 2026-11-10, after [PR #2383](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2383>) merged (09:35) but before it deployed (09:44). The block above was rendered from the old template, so it still tells the run to merge its own PR and move this task to Done. That finish line no longer applies. Ruling `lin4390-stage2-end-owner` (decision `8810f969` on LIN-4390) settles it for every Periodical:

* Do steps 1–8 and the adversarial second read as written, up to a green, rebased docs-only PR. **Do not merge it, and do not move this task to Done.**
* Post the PR-URL comment, then the three-field second-read comment, then a closing comment with the severity-ranked summary. That comment names who finishes: review approves, then close-out merges the PR, sets this task to Done and posts the final summary.
* Leave the task **In Progress**. "Do not leave the task open" above now means: hand it to review and close-out. Do not leave it with no named next step.

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Delivers the run 7 review report and its area-note edits in one green docs-only pull request as asked; no Survey finding binds, since template growth, triplicated API docs and the registry's doc gap are deeper and stay in the report.
**Cuts:**

* "Merge the report PR once its required checks are green.": close-out merges, per the LIN-4390 ruling.
* "Move this task to Done.": close-out sets Done, per the LIN-4390 ruling.
  **Decided by:** a ruling

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out (2026-11-10). The research findings and the full plan are discharged.*

fits one session

plan-review due: no

**Implemented as approved, with no deviations:** the Documentation Review run 7 report (docs/reviews/documentation-review-2026-11-10.md) and its area-note edits, merged as [PR #2392](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2392>) (merge commit 80f4c7c87), after six review-requested doc fixes (F1 to F6, commit d3c7465a4) and green CI on that commit. The full pre-prune description is preserved in the task snapshots, and the research, plan, review and close-out history is in the comment trail.

comments.body: **Finish line corrected (LIN-4390).** This task was minted in the gap between PR #2383's merge (09:35 UTC) and its deploy (09:44 UTC), so the sealed `## As asked` block carries the retired self-finish contract: "merge it", "Move this task to Done". Under ruling `lin4390-stage2-end-owner`, the run stops at a green, rebased PR plus its PR-URL, second-read and closing hand-off comments. Review approves, and close-out merges and sets Done. I added a `## Finish line superseded (LIN-4390)` section below the block saying so; the block itself is unchanged. Close-out of LIN-4390 also verified that a fresh mint renders the new wording: at `f5b1f5ef`, 32/32 Periodical renders carry "neither merges nor moves the task to Done".

## Survey open-0: LIN-4406 @ f5b1f5efa

`origin/main` is `f5b1f5efa`, the minting HEAD itself, so the LV window really is 461 commits / 5,505 files. SD `origin/main` is still `5d8489e`.

**Why this will be difficult**

1. **The scope is several runs' worth, and the brief then says widen it.** It covers two repos, the new area notes, the seal / size / leftover surfaces, new routes, the guide (204 KB), the unswept `public/llms.txt` (127 KB), SD's README (35 KB), and 18 carried-forward findings. A full sweep comes back shallow. The deeper symptom: the template gains surfaces every run and never drops one. That is the inflation this review exists to flag.

2. **The minting spot checks are already partly stale.** #3 is gone: `CLAUDE.md` no longer says "static projects preview", so LIN-2391 may be settled. #2 holds, and it is sharper than stated: `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` itself says the kit heartbeat is "not sent", while `docs/dispatch-integration.md` says the kit sends it. #5 holds (0 hits). Re-execute every claim.

3. **The findings land in notes that are full.** Through `areas.json`, the leftover finding's home is `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` → llm-and-prompts (6,142 B). The heartbeat finding's home is `lib/runner-kit/contract.json` → runs-and-dispatch (6,143 B). Both are within 2 B of the cap, so every entry needs a prune first. `public/llms.txt` maps to front-end-browser, an odd home for an agent doc. Placement will cost more than finding. It is also circular: the review judges these notes for inflation while it is required to add to them.

4. **The likely top finding is an absence.** `leftover` is a live kind (`ROW_ONLY_KINDS` = `['wake','leftover']`, executed). Yet "leftover" / `LEFTOVER_RULE` get 0 hits in `lib/proxy-instructions.js`, `docs/proxy-integration.md`, `public/llms.txt` and `CLAUDE.md`. "As asked" and "Size of the move" appear in the guide only. Checking claims against code won't find this; you have to go from the code to the docs.

5. **The finish line is contradictory.** The sealed `## As asked` says merge and Done, and the LIN-4390 block below it overrides that. `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` only checks for a GitHub URL and the three second-read fields, so a run that follows the sealed text literally can still satisfy the gate and merge too early.

6. **The two area READMEs have drifted.** LV is 4,217 B, SD is 3,885 B, about 25% similar by character. The shared rules may now differ between the repos.

**What I'd do first**

- Triage. Re-run the 18 carry-forwards mechanically, retire the ones already fixed, and give each ticketed one a single row.
- Go deep on three surfaces and label the rest "spot-checked": the leftover / seal absence; the area notes in both repos (against code, with the guards run); `public/llms.txt`.
- Before writing anything, pick the settled Lessons in the two capped notes to prune.
- Record the template's own growth (`lib/periodicals.js`) as a finding.

## Survey global: LIN-4406 @ f5b1f5efa

(SD read at `5d8489e7f`.)

**Where it lands.** Two kinds of doc surface. The **area notes** (LV: 12 notes plus a README; SD: 5 plus a README) are new, guarded by `tests/unit/area-notes.test.js` (slug, path exists, first path in the right area, 6,144 B cap) and well tended, with 39 commits in the window. They are getting better. The **stores** keep growing and nobody prunes them: `docs/reviews/` holds 109 top-level reports and 45 evidence dirs (91 MB) with no index, `source-map.md` is 193 KB, and `docs/proxy-integration.md` (204 KB) and `public/llms.txt` (127 KB) both restate `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (135 KB). LV `CLAUDE.md` is at 11,976 of its 12,000 B. The stores are getting worse.

**Done the obvious way:**
- **Adds report #110** (and maybe evidence dir #46) to a store with no index.
- **Funnels into the two full notes.** The registry gives docs no home, so a finding cites the code that owns the doc. The gate codes go through `lib/periodical-report-gate.js` to runs-and-dispatch (6,143 B). The As-asked, leftover and periodical wording goes through `lib/periodicals.js` and `lib/prompts/leftover-words.js` to llm-and-prompts (6,142 B). Every entry added there must be paid for in pruned bytes. Its five "Survey tally" entries are the first candidates.
- **Misfiles `public/llms.txt`.** The `^public/` pattern puts it in front-end-browser, so an entry about llms.txt drift would be read by people changing browser JS, not by whoever changes the catalog it copies (agent-api). The guard checks bytes and paths, not who will read an entry.
- **Risks putting items in two places.** Several carried findings already have tickets (LIN-2390, 3115, 3116, 3636, 4320). Under `LEFTOVER_RULE` they stay in the report only, not in a note. Some of the brief's spot checks are already stale: #3's "static projects preview" has 0 hits in `CLAUDE.md` at BASE. #2 (`runner/heartbeat`, 1 hit) and #5 (both gate codes, 0 hits across the catalog, guide and llms.txt) still hold.
- **Small:** one runs-and-dispatch Waiting entry (contract.json, Seams & Tangles) puts its report path on a trailing line outside the parenthesis, unlike the README format. SD's README is a declared copy of LV's format, and nothing compares the two.

**Better, at this task's cost:**
- Leave both capped notes net-zero or smaller. Prune settled entries and entries a ticket now owns before adding any.
- File catalog, guide and llms.txt drift under agent-api, citing `lib/proxy-instructions.js` first, and say in the report that the registry misplaces `public/llms.txt`.
- Write the `docs/reviews/` index (or archive-by-series) as one Waiting entry worded as a size of move, not as new prose.
- Re-verify every spot check and drop the ones already fixed.

**Better still, not this task's:**
- Give docs an owner mapping that leaves the code-shape census alone (the LIN-3829 caution), so doc findings stop leaking into the two busiest code notes.
- Generate llms.txt and the guide's route lists from `lib/proxy-instructions.js`. Today each run reviews three copies.
- Decide whether to generate or pin `source-map.md`.

This ticket treats drift, which is a symptom. Keeping three copies of the API docs makes the drift again after every review.

## Research notes: LIN-4406 @ LV `ecabd3d76` / SD `5d8489e7f`

**Stage:** research only. Nothing written to either repo, no PR, no note edits. This sets up the report-writing stage.
**Method:** the main session plus three fresh-context fork reads (the SD side, the 18 carry-forwards, and the API docs against the new features). Counts were executed, not grepped; the catalog was rendered with `buildInstructions()`. The top finding, the `llms.txt` premise and the `SIZE_RECORD_SHAPE` gap were re-run in the main session.

### Re-grounding (staleness check)

* LV `origin/main` has moved **four commits past minting** (`f5b1f5efa` → `ecabd3d76`, LIN-4404 #2386). The window is now **465 commits (427 non-merge), 5,509 files**. Per area, through the executed `docs/areas/areas.json` `match`: runs-and-dispatch 79, front-end-pages 74, front-end-browser 73, llm-and-prompts 55, web-routes 37, auth 33, agent-api 27, **other-features 21** (was 20), reports 13, providers 11, platform 7, task-model 2, wiring 1. Unmapped: 5,076, of which `docs/reviews` 2,780, `docs/papers` 1,143, `tests/unit` 720. LIN-4404 also touched `docs/areas/agent-api.md` (a `/cost` Lesson) and the `/cost` text in the catalog and guide.
* SD has had no commits since minting: **67 commits, 255 files**. test-harnesses 50, state-and-config 9, launch-and-harnesses 6, stop-hook-and-relay 6, reapers-and-liveness 5, loop-and-routing 3, plus 161 unit tests, 12 docs and 3 root files.
* **Seed corrections:**
  1. #3's CLAUDE.md landing wording is fixed. `CLAUDE.md:69` matches `lib/render-landing.js:1-15`, rewritten in LIN-3980 (`c93e2d41b`). **LIN-2391 is still Backlog**, and its title (Jira read-only, no-OAuth, proxy framing) is wider than that one line, so cite it and don't retire it.
  2. **`public/llms.txt` is not a third copy of the API docs.** It is the browser and DOM guide (Navigation, DOM Structure, Selectors…). It names 5 of 79 proxy paths and mentions `api/proxy` on 2 lines. The "three overlapping API surfaces" framing in both Surveys is wrong: the overlap is **two** surfaces (the catalog and the guide). The registry's `^public/` → front-end-browser placement is **correct**, so don't file llms.txt drift under agent-api.
  3. The "five Survey tally entries" are in **runs-and-dispatch (6)**, not llm-and-prompts (1).
  4. `areas.json` has **13** areas (the 10-21 report said 12).

### Per-layer audit (sources cited at HEAD)

**L1 · Served catalog `lib/proxy-instructions.js` (agent-api).** It covers 67 of 79 registered proxy paths. Missing: 4 legacy aliases, 4 session-auth token routes, the `cycle/:id` alias, `/issues/{id}/snapshots`, `/snapshots/diff` and `/issues/{id}/prompt/{templateKey}` (`routes/proxy-compute.js:283`). Ten proxy routes were added in the window, none removed; all 10 are in the catalog. It interpolates the As-asked and size-record words from `lib/as-asked.js` and `lib/size-of-move.js` (`SIZE_RECORD_CODES`, 4 of 4). Gaps:
* `leftover` has 0 hits, and nothing describes the held DONE wake. The catalog tells an orchestrator it is woken on DONE (`:937`), but for a stage `implementation` build that wake is held until the `leftover` row ends (`lib/dispatch-leftover.js:1-17`, `lib/dispatch-leftover-hook.js`). The only description is in the developer doc `docs/architecture/dispatch-and-proxy.md:117-123`.
* The `kind` contract (`:885`) says "prompt-template keys plus custom". Executed, `DISPATCH_KINDS` has 23 entries, including `defer`, `autopilot` and `periodical`. Rows read back can carry `ROW_ONLY_KINDS` = `['wake','leftover']` (`lib/dispatch-fields.js:188`, executed).
* The two periodical gate codes have 0 hits (`lib/periodical-report-gate.js:125,139`, a 409 on PATCH-to-Done from `routes/proxy-writes.js:473`; LIN-2390).
* The `readWrite`+`take` grants row (`:1036`) is unmintable, since `RUNNER_GRANTS` = `['take','dispatch']` (`lib/proxy-scopes.js:29`).
* The poll entry (`:1059`) doesn't state the `isRunnerTarget` restriction (`routes/proxy-runner.js:120-124`).
* `effort` is not in the POST /dispatch body (`:877`; accepted at `lib/dispatch-entrance.js:278`; LIN-2656).
* The verb override lists 15 of 19 `PROMPT_TEMPLATES` (`:954`; D&C row 131, LIN-4302).
* "60/min **per token**" appears 3 times (`:46`, `:1155`, `:1208`). Code keys on a *proven* credential and falls back to the IP (`routes/proxy.js:236-262`), so this is wrong for first requests and bootstrap exchanges. The guide has it right.
